messages:
Elaine: FYI escalated from Acme — prod streaming session (SSE) cuts off right after an auth rotate. Customer sees a bunch of valid JSON events, then connection closes and the final object is missing. No finish_reason in the last delivered fragment. request_id=req_0a1b2c, model=redwood-large-v1, region=us-west-2

Support Bot: Ticket created #SUP-4392 — attaching what customer sent.

Tomas: Can you paste the raw SSE frames / curl trace? Need to know whether the last frame was partially sent (trailing comma / open brace) or if the server never emitted the terminal event. Also want proxy logs around the same time.

Elaine: Pasting trimmed traces from the customer (they scrubbed tokens):
```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked

data: {"id":"tok1","text":"Hello world\n"}

data: {"id":"tok2","text":"More text"}

data: {"id":"tok3","text":"Final part, should include finish_reason"}

# connection drops here, browser shows EOF
```
Client reconnect attempt (browser auto-retry):
```
GET /v1/streams/resume?session=req_0a1b2c HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Last-Event-ID: tok3

# server returns 200 with a small heartbeat then nothing else; no terminal event appended
```
Customer curl (repro):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  'https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-large-v1' --no-buffer
```

Marco: Infra look — from our edge logs I see a connection CLOSE (RST) from the client at ~15:42:13 while the upstream returned 200 and wrote the last chunk at ~15:42:12. There's an auth refresh flow (401 -> token swap -> 200) happening within that same window. Fastly/edge has idle/keepalive behavior that can tear down the TCP connection when a backend auth handoff occurs. It looks like the final chunk was accepted by the upstream runtime but not flushed to the downstream connection before the edge closed it. Also we don't set Content-Length for chunked SSE, so partial buffered bytes can be lost on abrupt close.

Li: Oncall workaround for customer: 1) enable 'stable-session' flag in their tenant which defers auth rotation until stream finalization (we can toggle for them short-term); 2) client-side: when resuming, request last ~512 tokens by re-sending a delta prompt (instead of relying purely on resume token) so missing tail can be reconstructed. Both are safe short-term workarounds.

Tomas: Proposed engineering fix: two parts — (A) runtime must always emit an explicit terminal SSE event before allowing token rotation / auth swap. Example sentinel: `event: done\ndata: {"finish_reason":"stop"}\n\n` — this gives clients a deterministic end. (B) edge/proxy: add tiny tail-buffering window (buffer final 64KB per stream) and ensure buffer is flushed atomically on connection close or replayed on resume requests. I'll open an RFC + low-risk patch: buffer-and-flush + guard around auth rotations for active streams.

Elaine: Customer confirmed the stable-session toggle fixed their immediate failures. They've accepted an engineering debug session next week. @Tomas please open the PR and add an integration test that simulates an auth rotate mid-stream and asserts the terminal sentinel is delivered.

Tomas: Will do. I'll include a repro test that runs a local proxy which sends a simulated RST during the last chunk and assert resume returns terminal event. :thumbsup:

Marco: I'll follow up with a Fastly config proposal for increasing our idle timeout for live SSE paths and gating token swap until final flush.

Li: Marking SUP-4392 as in-progress. If anyone oncall wants to pair with the customer this afternoon let me know.

Elaine: Thanks all, updating customer.
